terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: Not solved; fixed by the consumer harness.

objectClass.primaryType: small mound of shredded dried coconut
objectClass.notes: Matte faceted clay shading. CRIB top risk category (thin scattered strands + near-background body color) -- mitigated with a generously-sized toasted color bucket rather than relying on the near-white body hue alone.

reasoning: Silhouette 2: a loose scatter reads as noise, not a pile -- readability depends entirely on overlap density, which required 5 revision rounds to reach (see risks).

Repetition density 2: 28 shred instances across 3 layers, higher than the batch's typical 3-instance clusters, placed by a procedural layer-based formula rather than hand-authored per instance (rosemary needle-cluster precedent).

materialLayerCount 1: two color buckets (ivory body, toasted flecks), no texture -- unlike lemon/banana in the same batch, coconut carries no per-strand texture (would be over-budget for this many small parts).
Occlusion risk 2: dense overlapping strands in a genuine 3D heap occlude each other more than a flat cluster of discrete bodies.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Simple tier by part count, but needs a repetitionSystem for the layered shred mound and a representative meso component rather than per-instance authoring (rosemary pattern).

detailInventory.note: Enumerated by hand from the three reference views (CRIB.md skip rule).

details.observation: A minority of strands (tips or whole pieces) are toasted golden-brown against the near-white majority.
details.inference: Primary color-contrast cue -- CRIB-flagged risk: the ivory body hex (#EFE6D2) is within 3-4 RGB units of the card background (#F2E6D3), so the toasted bucket carries most of the against-background legibility.

details.observation: Pile has real 3D height, denser/narrower toward the top, wider/lower at the base.
details.inference: Distinguishes a heap from a flat scatter; low-poly budget forces far fewer, chunkier strands than the reference's fine weave.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

mustMatch: a compact, densely overlapping mound (not a sparse scatter)
toasted-brown flecks visibly contrasting against the pale ivory majority
niceToHave: exact strand count/curl matching the reference's fine weave -- explicitly out of reach for a <=700tri budget

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

featureReviewTargets.name: Reads as a compact overlapping mound, not scattered confetti
Toasted flecks provide visible contrast against the pale majority and the card background

sculptPipeline.blockedReason: blockout requires a browser screenshot and self-correction review before structural-pass unlocks

critical semantic feature scores from the same image pair meeting their individual thresholds

droppedPasses.lighting-pass: lighting is fixed by the consumer harness and is not authorable in the model
droppedPasses.interaction-pass: static showcase prop with no sockets, hinges or colliders beyond a bounding proxy

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: Consumer runtime keeps only map and color; PBR maps are inert.

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold

lightingPass.authority: Lighting is fixed by the consumer harness.

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

assumptions: The runtime normalizes the pile's longest axis to 1.6.
Exact strand count/weave is not achievable at this tri budget; the review scores overall mound cohesion and color contrast, not per-strand fidelity.

coordinateFrame.front: +Z, the direction the harness three-quarter camera looks from
coordinateFrame.scaleReference: SCATTER radii (0.12-0.30) are relative units. Absolute scale is meaningless (types.ts section 6).

silhouette.boundingShape: low 3-layer mound of overlapping shred chips, roughly 0.7 wide by 0.35 tall by 0.7 deep in relative units
silhouette.symmetry: no strong symmetry -- procedural per-layer angular scatter
negativeSpaces: gaps between overlapping shreds -- minimized across 5 revision rounds
landmarks: scattered toasted-brown flecks against the pale majority

observations: a dense, tightly woven low mound of thin curled ivory-white coconut shreds, overlapping and crossing at many angles with almost no visible background between them
scattered strand tips and a handful of whole flecks are toasted a light-to-deep golden brown, standing out against the pale body
the pile has real height (a mound, not a flat scatter) -- strands stack in visible layers with a few tips lifting above the main mass
confirms individual strands are numerous and thin, packed edge-to-edge -- far denser than what a low-poly budget (<=700tri) can represent 1:1

componentTree.name: Coconut Shred Pile
componentTree.topologyRationale: Transform-only assembly node carrying the 28 shred instances across 3 layers; emits no geometry of its own.

collider.notes: Bounding proxy; sufficient for a static showcase prop.

colorMaterialRecipe.materialClassRationale: Matte faceted ingredient prop, opaque dielectric, roughness 1.0 -- reference/prompt JSON explicitly excludes shine.

localFeatures.name: 3-layer cairn-style mound
localFeatures.description: 3 concentric layers of decreasing radius and increasing height (0.30/0.14, 0.21/0.14, 0.12/0.26) -- a real 3D heap silhouette, grounded once at the pile's own lowest point (not per-shred).

surfaceDetail.occlusionPattern: none -- runtime Lambert has no AO channel
surfaceDetail.notes: Assembly node; no surface of its own.

componentTree.name: Shred (representative)
componentTree.topologyRationale: Each shred is a chain of 2 independent 4-vertex tetrahedra (root, tip, 2 wing points per segment) -- the same chunky 'always-visible-from-any-angle' technique as rosemary's needle, chosen specifically because a flat quad card would go invisible from back-facing angles under the runtime's single-sided material (types.ts, doubleSided does not survive the material swap). Represents the 28-instance repetitionSystem below; placement is procedural (3 layers x per-layer angle+radius+jitter), not hand-authored per instance.

deformationStack.notes: R4 (types.ts): shreds get zero vertex jitter, same reasoning as rosemary's needles -- thin geometry mangles under bread-scale noise. Curvature comes from the 1 gentle bend between the 2 chained segments, not per-vertex noise.

geometryDescriptor.uvStrategy: top-planar (scripts/breads/lib.ts uvTopPlanar) -- solid color, UV only for merge attribute consistency
geometryDescriptor.normalStrategy: flat normals via facet() on each segment's raw tetrahedron

attachment.notes: Each instance's root is placed by the layer distribution formula below; the whole pile is grounded once (bounding-box Y correction on the top-level group), not per-shred -- per-shred grounding would flatten the intentional layer heights.

collider.notes: Bounding proxy; sufficient for a static showcase prop.

colorMaterialRecipe.materialClassRationale: Matte faceted ingredient prop, opaque dielectric, roughness 1.0 -- reference/prompt JSON explicitly excludes shine.

localFeatures.name: One gentle bend, not a straight card
localFeatures.description: 1st segment nearly horizontal, 2nd segment bends by 0.12-0.42 rad (one bend only, not per-segment random zigzag -- v3 revision after cmp-2 read as disconnected diamonds).

surfaceDetail.normalPattern: flat normals from facet(), each tetrahedron's 4 faces give independent shading per angle
surfaceDetail.occlusionPattern: none -- runtime Lambert has no AO channel
surfaceDetail.notes: Ivory or toasted material chosen per-shred (whole-shred) or per-tip-segment (partial), not painted.

materials.name: Shred body (ivory)

textureProjection.texelDensityIntent: No texture emitted; UVs exist only for merge attribute consistency (types.ts section 4).

textureProjection.texelDensityIntent: No texture emitted; UVs exist only for merge attribute consistency (types.ts section 4).

roughness.localResponse: inert -- runtime Lambert swap discards roughness

displacement.pattern: toasted shred tips + whole toasted flecks

localOverrides.name: Generous toasted-bucket share
localOverrides.description: 15% of shreds fully toasted (simulating scattered whole flecks) + 35% tip-only toasted (2-segment chain, so this colors half of that shred) -- deliberately larger than the prompt's 'a few' flecks would suggest, to compensate for the near-background ivory hue (advisor-flagged risk).

shaderNotes: Emit via scripts/breads/lib.ts stdMaterial(): MeshStandardMaterial roughness 1, metalness 0.
materials.notes: toasted shred tips + whole toasted flecks.

repetitionSystems.name: Shred mound system

distribution.mode: 3 concentric layers (y=0.0/r=0.30/n=11, y=0.14/r=0.21/n=9, y=0.26/r=0.12/n=8), each shred's root placed at angle=(i/count)*2pi+jitter, radius=layer.radius*(0.35+0.65*rng) biased toward the layer center
distribution.note: 5 total revision rounds (3 numbered cmp + 2 further passes verified via production thumb bake): v1 wide spiral scatter (r=0.82) read as scattered confetti; v2 layered but still sparse/necked joints; v3 fewer/wider segments (3->2) fixed joint necking but the shred length (0.4-0.58) still exceeded the shrunken layer radii, creating a spiky starburst; v4 shortened shred length to match layer radii (0.2-0.32), finally giving a compact overlapping mound.

repetitionSystems.seedRule: Per-instance angle jitter, radius, category (ivory/tip-toast/full-toast) and bend angle all consume the builder rng (mulberry32); deterministic, byte-stable GLB export.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Cluster group target 300-700tri/<=68KB (CRIB) -- measured 224tri/23.1KB, below the floor but accepted per CRIB precedent (rosemary 108tri): '64px readability is the judge, not the target floor.'

lightingFromPhoto.exposure: no exposure control or tone mapping.

lightingFromPhoto.observation: Cool directional fill opposite the key.
lightingFromPhoto.toneMapping: NoToneMapping; no AO on runtime Lambert.

proceduralStrategy: Build each shred as a chain of 2 independent 4-vertex tetrahedra (rosemary needle technique, local reimplementation) with one gentle bend between segments (not per-segment random zigzag).
Scatter shreds across 3 concentric layers of decreasing radius and increasing height for a cairn-style mound silhouette.
Keep shred length comparable to the layer radius so shreds stay within the mound's footprint instead of poking out as spikes (v4 fix).
Ground the whole pile once via a single bounding-box Y correction on the top-level group -- never per-shred (would flatten the intentional layer heights).
Assign material per-shred (15% fully toasted) or per-tip-segment (35% tip-toasted) via rng, generously sized to compensate for the near-background ivory hue.
animationAnchors: root pivot supports whole-pile rotation for the showcase turntable
destructionAnchors: single static prop; no plausible break beyond the whole object

risks.description: Body hex #EFE6D2 is within 3-4 RGB units of the card background #F2E6D3 -- the highest background-collision risk in the batch (advisor-flagged before implementation).
risks.mitigation: Toasted bucket sized generously (50% of shreds carry some toasted color, well above the prompt's 'a few flecks') plus faceted per-tetrahedron shading naturally darkens many facets under the key light, both giving luminance separation from the flat unlit card background even where hue alone would not.

risks.description: cmp-1/cmp-2 (wide spiral scatter, then layered-but-still-sparse) both read as scattered confetti/starburst rather than a pile -- the single most iteration-heavy asset in the batch (5 total revision rounds vs the CRIB 3-cmp guideline).
risks.mitigation: Root-caused via the production thumb-bake pipeline (not more cmp renders, which were budget-exhausted): shred length must be comparable to the pile's own footprint radius, not independent of it -- runtime auto-refit means absolute scale is meaningless but the *ratio* between part length and cluster radius determines whether parts stay within the silhouette or poke out as spikes.

risks.description: At 64px the pile reads as 'a small pale/brown clump' but may not be specifically identified as coconut shred without the item-name label the digest UI always shows alongside cards.
risks.mitigation: Accepted -- CRIB precedent (cinnamon) documents this exact honest limitation for fine-texture ingredients at thumbnail scale; the label closes the gap in the actual UI.

risks.description: flatShading not inherited by the runtime material swap.
risks.mitigation: facet() bakes flat normals into each tetrahedron segment.
